overview: This 154-page file documents public health and welfare in occupied Japan from 1947 to 1948. It combines correspondence about proposed compulsory health insurance, SCAP bulletins and disease reports, plans for welfare administration, a Rockefeller Foundation demographic survey, and charts tracking hospitals, nutrition, public assistance, vital statistics, and medical supplies.
interest: Prefectural disease data and production charts sit alongside policy debates, revealing how occupation officials measured and reshaped Japan’s welfare system.
